title: Unsubsidised RON95 and diesel down 15 sen, RON97 falls 20 sen for Nov 19-25
text:
Unsubsidised RON95 and diesel down 15 sen, RON97 falls 20 sen for Nov 19-25 Thursday 19 Nov 2026 BURSA SGX Home 
 Petrol Price Make The Edge Malaysia your preferred source on Google KUALA LUMPUR (Nov 18): The price of unsubsidised RON95 petrol and diesel will decline by 15 sen per litre, while RON97 petrol will fall by 20 sen per litre from Nov 19 to 25 amid easing global oil prices.
 RON97 drops 4.76% to RM4.00 per litre from RM4.20, while unsubsidised RON95 falls 3.88% to RM3.72 per litre from RM3.87, the Ministry of Finance (MOF) said in a statement on Wednesday.
 The price of unsubsidised diesel will decrease by 3.08% to RM4.72 per litre from RM4.87.
 In the statement, the MOF said moderation in global crude oil prices and expectations of higher global supply have eased price pressures in the international petroleum market.
 However, refined petroleum product supplies continue to face several constraints that could affect market price stability, alongside geopolitical uncertainties and shipping disruption risks that may keep global oil prices volatile in the near term.
 At the time of writing on Wednesday, Brent crude oil was trading at US$92.71 per barrel.
 Meanwhile, eligible recipients under the Budi Madani RON95 (Budi95) programme will continue to pay RM1.99 per litre. The government subsidy amounts to RM2.28 per litre, or 53% of the unsubsidised price.
 Recipients under the Budi Madani Diesel programme will continue to pay RM2.10 per litre, representing a government subsidy of RM3.02 per litre, or 59% of the unsubsidised price.
 The subsidised prices under the Subsidised Petrol Control System (SKPS) and Subsidised Diesel Control System (SKDS) will remain unchanged at RM2.05 and RM2.15 per litre respectively.
 The MOF reiterated the government's commitment to protecting households and businesses from global fuel price volatility through targeted subsidies.
 As announced in Budget 2027, fuel subsidies are expected to remain at around RM40 billion next year to help ease cost-of-living pressures.
